skill.name: helm-chart-scaffolding
skill.description: Create, organize, validate, and document Helm charts for Kubernetes applications using reusable scaffolds and production-oriented patterns.
skill.summary: Scaffold Helm charts with Kubernetes templates, values files, dependencies, and validation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Helm examples, documentation URLs, Markdown code spans, and an optional local validation script. One semantic issue remains: PostgreSQL examples use a default password of changeme, which can become an insecure credential if copied into production. No prompt injection, covert network call, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Default PostgreSQL password in scaffold examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace changeme with a required placeholder, generated secret reference, or external secret manager guidance.

remediation.issue: Plaintext environment value examples may be misused for secrets
remediation.suggestion: Show valueFrom and Kubernetes Secret references for sensitive variables, and keep .Values.env for non-sensitive settings.

remediation.issue: Optional validation script runs local Helm commands
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should review charts and dependencies before running the script in an environment with cluster credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Default Database Password in Scaffold
semantic_findings.description: The values template and playbook include password: changeme for PostgreSQL. Users could copy this scaffold and deploy a database with a predictable password.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited lines define the PostgreSQL auth password as changeme in reusable chart examples. This is a clear insecure-default risk if users copy the scaffold without replacing it.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent Helm charts is slow and error-prone for teams packaging Kubernetes applications. This skill provides chart structure, templating guidance, validation steps, and repository patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains standard Helm chart directory structure and required files.
Provides Chart.yaml and values.yaml scaffolding patterns.
Guides creation of Kubernetes manifest templates and helper templates.
Describes dependency configuration for PostgreSQL and Redis examples.
Includes validation workflows for linting, rendering, and dry-run checks.
Covers chart packaging, repository indexing, and multi-environment values.
limitations: Does not deploy applications or verify live cluster behavior by itself.
Requires the user to review generated values for security and environment fit.
Example dependencies and URLs must be replaced with project-specific sources.
Validation scripts depend on local Helm, jq, and Kubernetes tooling availability.

use_cases.title: Create a New Application Chart
use_cases.description: Generate a chart layout, metadata, values, and starter templates for a new Kubernetes service.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Chart Patterns
use_cases.description: Align team charts around shared labels, helpers, resource settings, ingress, probes, and dependency conventions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Chart for Release
use_cases.description: Review packaging steps, dependency handling, repository indexing, and validation commands before publishing a chart.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Helm chart scaffold for my Kubernetes application. Ask for missing chart name, image, service port, and maintainer details before drafting files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Production Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design values.yaml for a production Helm chart with replicas, resources, probes, ingress, service account settings, and optional persistence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Chart Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Helm chart templates for naming, labels, helper usage, values validation, and compatibility with multiple Kubernetes environments.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Release Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a validation plan for publishing this Helm chart, including linting, rendering, dry-run checks, dependency review, documentation, and repository indexing.

output_examples.input: I need a Helm chart for a small web API with PostgreSQL and ingress.
output_examples.output: A chart plan with metadata, values sections, deployment and service templates, optional PostgreSQL dependency settings, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review my chart before I publish it to an internal repository.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering dependencies, schema validation, package commands, repository indexing, and warnings about insecure defaults.

output_examples.input: Help me support dev, staging, and production values files.
output_examples.output: A multi-environment structure with shared defaults, environment overrides, deployment guidance, and validation commands for each environment.

best_practices: Replace all placeholder URLs, maintainers, image names, and dependency settings before publishing a chart.
Validate charts with linting, template rendering, and dry-run checks before release.
Use Kubernetes Secrets or external secret managers for sensitive values.
anti_patterns: Do not ship charts with default passwords or copied example credentials.
Do not hardcode environment-specific hostnames, namespaces, or storage classes in shared defaults.
Do not run validation scripts against unreviewed charts or unknown dependency sources.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Helm chart structure, metadata, values files, templates, dependencies, validation steps, and release documentation.

faq.question: Can it deploy my chart to a cluster?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and optional validation commands, but deployment still requires user approval and local tooling.

faq.question: Does it support multi-environment charts?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains shared defaults, separate values files, and validation for development, staging, and production environments.

faq.question: Are the example URLs ready for production?
faq.answer: No. They are examples and placeholders. Replace them with trusted repositories, project links, and approved dependency sources.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use Kubernetes Secrets, existing secret references, or an external secret manager. Do not store real secrets in default values files.
